content:
I just discovered that if a module declares a private instance, and a non-module imports that file, then this private instance is available to type class search there. I found this in #36468, which had an extremely confusing failure in one of the Counterexamples files (which is still a non-module).

Would it make sense to ignore all private declarations when exporting instances? (cc @Sebastian Ullrich)
Hmm, but a non-module does import the private interface, just like import all, which presumably should also be able to see the instance
So, we should be using private local instance rather than private instance?
Is this a regression? Before the advent of the module system, private declarations weren't accessible from downstream files
One might reasonably think so, but I don't think this has ever been true in Lean 4 for instances
